text:
sara: quick help — Marta moved from Berlin to Lisbon and switched payroll mid-pay period. She relocated on 2024-08-14; pay period is 2024-08-01 -> 2024-08-31. Contract switched to PT payroll effective 2024-08-15. How should we handle income tax and social contributions for the August payrun and year-end docs?

oliver_payroll: short answer: split the period and run two payslips (DE for 8/1-8/14, PT for 8/15-8/31). need to confirm: 1) Marta's official tax residency change date, 2) whether employer continued DE SS for the first half, 3) any A1 or social security certificates. do we have her de-registration (Abmeldung)?

juan_pp: @sara Marta said she deregistered Berlin (Abmeldung) on 2024-08-14 and registered in PT on 2024-08-15. Sent NIF and temporary residency note. No A1 on file.

oliver_payroll: ok. Without an A1, German social security likely applies up to 8/14 (employee + employer). PT contributions from 8/15 onwards. For taxes: DE taxes income earned while resident/working there; PT taxes income for the later period. avoid double-withholding for same income.

marta: i asked my manager about A1 — they said this is long-term so they didn't request one, sorry.

oliver_payroll: fine. Action items: 1) create two payslips for Aug (DE gross 1–14, PT gross 15–31). 2) collect proof of de-registration/registration. 3) run retro if DE payroll didn't withhold correctly. 4) flag for local tax filing guidance.

sara: how do we split numbers? prorate by days or working days?

oliver_payroll: we prorate by calendar days unless contract says otherwise. Example:

monthly_gross: €6,000
period_DE_days: 14 => DE_gross = 6000 * 14/31 = €2709.68
period_PT_days: 17 => PT_gross = 6000 * 17/31 = €3290.32

oliver_payroll: social security: calculate DE contributions on DE_gross, PT on PT_gross. check year-to-date ceilings/manual review.

juan_pp: year-end docs: Germany issues Lohnsteuerbescheinigung for DE period; Portugal issues reporting for PT period. We'll provide combined earnings summary for Marta for cross-border filing.

marta: will this affect my end-of-year filings? i usually file in DE — do i need to include PT income?

juan_pp: likely yes — you may need to file in both and claim foreign tax credits. recommend a local tax advisor. we'll provide payroll docs and day-split evidence.

oliver_payroll: ops next steps (assigned to Payroll Ops): - upload Marta's Abmeldung and PT registration - create DE payslip for 1–14 (run retro if needed) - create PT payslip for 15–31 on PT tenant and use NIF - update HRIS: tax residency change date = 2024-08-15 - add note for year-end docs and prepare combined earnings summary PDF

payroll-bot: PAYROLL_RUN CHECK — DE retro-run queued (job id: pr-202408-170406). ETA 2 business days.

sara: thanks. who should i loop in for legal/compliance on social security risk?

oliver_payroll: loop in paula_compliance and EMEA legal; ping PT payroll vendor for nuance on contribution ceilings. i'll create the ticket and tag people-ops.

juan_pp: i'll DM Marta the checklist of docs to upload. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
